headlines: POSSIBLE DOUBLE SHOOTING UNDER INVESTIGATION AT HIALEAH APARTMENT COMPLEX
GUNFIRE AND SCREAMS ROCK HIALEAH NEIGHBORHOOD
WHAT HAPPENED INSIDE A NORMALLY QUIET HIALEAH APARTMENT?
draft.article:
Hialeah police and fire rescue crews responded to an apartment complex near West 22nd Court and 61st Street following a possible double shooting. Surveillance footage from the area recorded screams alongside what sounded like gunfire.

First responders airlifted at least one patient on a stretcher via helicopter. On the second floor, investigators focused on a corner unit cordoned off with crime scene tape. An unnamed resident stated that her husband was shot and is currently recovering in a local hospital.

Neighbors reported seeing a late-night gathering turn into pushing and heated arguments before two injured men emerged. Authorities have not yet disclosed the full number of injuries or whether any suspects are in custody.

Inside, a sergeant had to perform sternum rubs to awaken the mother, Maria Jose Cortez Espinoza, who was surrounded by five open Sutter Home wine bottles. Hialeah police arrested Cortez Espinoza for child neglect without great bodily harm. She was booked into the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center near Doral on a $2,500 bond with an immigration hold.

headlines: TWO MEN ARRESTED FOR RAPING MIAMI-DADE TEEN IN HOLLYWOOD
TWO BROWARD MEN JAILED IN TEEN SEXUAL ASSAULT
MIAMI GARDENS TEEN ATTACKED AFTER MEETING MAN FROM APP
draft.article:
Two Broward County men are in custody following the sexual assault of a 17-year-old Miami-Dade girl who agreed to meet someone from a social app in Miami Gardens.

Miami Gardens police met the teenager on January 17 at Jackson Memorial Hospital's Roxcy Bolton Rape Treatment Center. Investigators learned she met 22-year-old Samauri Moton at Buccaneer Park on January 16 at 9:30 p.m. Moton brought her to Hollywood Beach at 3601 North Ocean Drive, accompanied by 25-year-old Jevaun Noel.

Authorities reported Noel assaulted the girl inside a parked vehicle while Moton waited outside. State DNA records matched Noel to the assault, leading to arrests by Hollywood police and Broward deputies.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE SHERIFF ASKS STATE FOR 42 MILLION DOLLARS MORE
COUNTY BUDGET BATTLE ERUPTS OVER MILLIONS
WHY SHERIFF ROSIE WANTS MORE CASH AMID CUTS
draft.article: Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz is seeking an additional $42 million from county funds after commissioners approved a record $1.2 billion department budget. To secure the funding for staffing, recruiting, and new stations, Cordero-Stutz asked Governor Ron DeSantis and the state Cabinet to intervene. The demand comes as Miami-Dade deals with service reductions, including cuts to late-night bus routes. The sheriff is also backing Amendment 3, a measure to cut property taxes that could cost the county $1.5 billion across 2028 and 2029. Amid budget tensions with Mayor Daniella Levine Cava, the sheriff announced plans to eliminate $4.1 million commissioner and mayoral security details starting November 9.

headlines: MIAMI ART WEEK AND NEW VENUES OPEN ACROSS OUR CITY
FRESH ATTRACTIONS AND DINING DEBUT IN MIAMI
EXPLORE NEW CULTURAL HOTSPOTS ACROSS GREATER MIAMI NEIGHBORHOODS
draft.article: Greater Miami and Miami Beach are welcoming fresh cultural spots, dining, and transit options ahead of Miami Art Week, running November 30 through December 6. New local highlights include the 8,000-square-foot Gibson Garage Miami, which opened in September with over 500 guitars and a live performance stage. In South Beach, the historic Royal Palm reopened following extensive renovations, while Lincoln Road added Sulta Rosa cafe, founded by dancers Daniella Karagach and Pasha Pashkov. Getting around remains accessible with complimentary Miami Beach and City of Miami trolleys alongside the weekday Biscayne Bay water taxi. Residents and visitors can also enjoy free jazz at The Betsy or watch domino matches at Maximo Gomez Park in Little Havana.
